thread:
Sam: FYI p99 spike on worker pool A again when training-like batches (4k+) interleave with short chat flows. Looking for fresh queueing ideas that don't require huge infra changes.
Priya: Can we try a ticketing system instead of strict lanes? requests buy "token-tickets" proportional to seq_length, scheduler fills cohorts by ticket budget rather than count. Short reqs get more tickets per token.
Diego: Interesting. So a 100-token request might consume 1 ticket unit while a 3k request consumes 30. Cohorts circulate when ticket budget full. That biases towards short ones for latency.
Noor: We need to bound worst-case: long requests could still starve if many shorts arrive. Add a decay/fairness parameter: long-requests accumulate priority over time (age-based bonus).
Sam: How do tickets map to GPU kernel efficiency? Big batches are cheaper per-token. We can't kill throughput entirely.
Priya: We set a min_long_fraction per cohort (e.g., 10%) to ensure background throughput. Also allow periodic "throughput windows" where scheduler favors high-token efficiency for N seconds.
Diego: Detector idea: infer kernel-time-per-token from recent cohorts; if tokens/second drops, shift cohort budget. That ties queueing to actual kernel utilization.
Noor: Telemetry we'll need: per-cohort average tokens, tokens/sec, cohort ticket composition, age distribution, KV cache warmness by cohort. Also breakpoint alerts when p99_fast > SLO and tokens/sec < expected.
Sam: Implementation complexity? ticket accounting + age boost + dynamic windowing seems doable in scheduler loop. But we should prototype in sim before touching prod.
Priya: I'll sketch sim config: arrival dist = mix of Exponential(short_mean=140) and Pareto(long_xm=1500, alpha=1.7). Ticket_unit = 100 tokens. cohort_ticket_budget = 50 units. age_bonus = 0.05 per second. throughput_window = 20s every 120s.
Diego: Edge-case: KV cache thrash when cohorts mix very different contexts. Maybe pin cohorts to affinity keys for KV cache locality: sticky-cohort-id for a brief TTL. That trades some mixing for higher cache-hit.
Noor: Also consider a fast-evict hint: if cohort has >N foreign contexts, drop oldest small requests to reclaim tickets and maintain latency. Need clear safety semantics.
Sam: Can we do soft early-reject for very large requests when fast ticket budget low? return 429 with Retry-After or suggest background endpoint. Less surprising for clients than huge latency.
Priya: Agree. Provide a graceful rejection policy: 429 + header X-Alternative-Endpoint: /batching. Docs must list idempotency expectations.
Diego: Security/ops: need feature-flag and a/b rollout. We'll start with sim -> canary (5% single-host) -> 25% -> roll. Add an emergency toggle to revert to FIFO.
Noor: One more thought: incorporate model parallelism hints. If model supports split-kernel for long sequences, mark request as 'parallelizable' and let scheduler pack it differently. Metadata field on request.
Sam: Good call. Add request.metadata: {"parallelizable":true, "affinity":"user-123"}.
infra-bot: infra: feature-flag created: ticket_cohort_experiment_v1=false. Canary playbook: docs/internal/playbooks/ticketing-canary.md created.
Priya: I'll write the RFC follow-up with design, sim results, and the exact config knobs: ticket_unit_size, cohort_ticket_budget, age_boost_rate, min_long_fraction, throughput_window_len, sticky_ttl.
Diego: I'll own a quick sim and a small scheduler implementation in staging. Expect PR tomorrow.
Sam: Thanks. Let's aim to validate: p50/p95/p99 by ticket-aged buckets, aggregate tokens/sec, and KV-hit delta. If sims look good we'll proceed. :rocket:
